title: LLM-IMC: Automating Analog In-Memory Computing Architecture Generation with Large Language Models
problem: The knowledge-intensive hardware design process and lack of high-quality circuit netlists constrain design space exploration and optimization of analog In-Memory Computing systems, limiting designs to behavioral system-level tools.
motivation: Resistive crossbars for analog IMC offer high memory access bandwidth and in-situ computing capabilities for DNN acceleration, making automated design exploration critical for practical deployment.
method: LLM-IMC is a fine-tune-free LLM framework that automates SPICE netlist generation for analog IMC through a Python-based tool. It systematically generates diverse IMC simulation scripts, performs LLM-driven performance analysis for design space exploration, and provides an integration roadmap for neuromorphic crossbar design flows.
key_novelty: Using a fine-tune-free LLM to automate SPICE netlist generation and performance analysis for analog in-memory computing architecture design.
contributions: Fine-tune-free LLM framework for automated SPICE code generation for analog IMC
Python-based tool for systematic creation of diverse IMC simulation scripts
LLM-driven performance analysis enabling efficient design space exploration
Integration roadmap for neuromorphic crossbar design flows
limitations: Experimental validation against existing design methodologies and quantitative performance comparisons not discussed.
primary_theme: LLM-driven automation of analog IMC circuit design
